# dmai 1.0.0

## Changes visible to users

* `dmai()` keeps its name, its arguments (`.data`, `method`, `logbase`) and its result (a table with the date and
  `DMAI`); new arguments are appended: `date`, `x`, `r` (column names; by default `Date`, `x1`, `x2`, ... and `r1`,
  `r2`, ... as before), `user_cost` (user costs given directly), `benchmark` (a benchmark rate instead of the
  largest component rate, with the upper envelope), `percent`, `base` and `as_dt`.
* The table also has the index level (`index`, equal to `base` at the first date) and `value` (the aggregate in
  the units of the components). It is a `data.table` (version 0.5.0 returned a grouped tibble).
* `as_dt = FALSE` returns the full result, of class `c("dmai_index", "dmai_result", "list")`: the index, the user
  costs and shares of every component, the benchmark rate, the dual user-cost price index, the Divisia second
  moments and the simple sum, with `print()`, `summary()`, `plot()`, `ggplot2::autoplot()` and `as.data.table()`
  methods; the printed result ends with the sources of the method.
* Every function that takes data or a result is an S3 generic with a `.default` method.
* `method` has a default (`"Barnett"`): in version 0.5.0 a call without `method` stopped with an error.

## Corrections

* The growth `DMAI` of the Barnett method used logarithms to base 10 by default (`logbase = NULL`), which gives
  0.434 times the growth rate; Barnett's Divisia index uses natural logarithms. The default is now the natural
  logarithm, so `DMAI` is the growth in percent; `logbase = 10` reproduces version 0.5.0 exactly.

## New

* Methods `"Fisher"` (Fisher ideal index), `"SimpleSum"` and `"CE"` (currency equivalent index of Rotemberg,
  Driscoll and Poterba 1995) in `dmai()`.
* `dmai_compare()`: every method on the same data, with average growth per period and per year.
* `dmai_user_cost()`: user costs and expenditure shares of the components.
* `dmai_moments()`: Divisia means and variances of the growth of the components and of their user costs (Barnett
  and Serletis 1990).
* The dual user-cost price index by factor reversal.
* `dmai_interpret()`, `dmai_cite()`, `dmai_app()`: a plain-language interpretation of every result, the references
  of every method and a built-in shiny application; `dmai_theme()`, `dmai_save()` (with WebP), `dmai_notation()`,
  `dmai_reference()`.
* Data: `money_sim` (simulated monthly monetary components, 2005 to 2024) and `cpi_ch19` (the artificial data of
  the Consumer Price Index Manual, whose chained Laspeyres, Paasche, Fisher and Tornqvist indexes the package
  reproduces).
* Quarto vignettes in HTML and PDF; complete help pages with the formulas; tests against version 0.5.0, hand
  computations and the published values.

## Internal

* dplyr, magrittr, stringr, tibble and tidyr are no longer imported; the computations are matrix operations and
  `data.table`.
